item.title: Outside 77 Heath street, 16th November
item.description:
I am writing to report an issue regarding road barriers left behind outside my business premises, Meekhun Thai Bistro, located at Heath Street, NW36UG, Hampstead. Although the roadworks on Heath Street were completed several months ago, a plastic road barrier has been abandoned directly in front of our restaurant entrance, as shown in the attached photos. This barrier has been left here for months and is causing a significant obstruction to the front of our shop, impacting pedestrian access and negatively affecting the appearance and operation of our business. Could you please arrange for the responsible team to collect and remove this barrier as soon as possible?

item.title: URGENT FORMAL COMPLAINT – Serious Ongoing Problems in Our Building.Woodsford Portland Street London., 16th November
item.description:
URGENT FORMAL COMPLAINT – Serious Ongoing Problems in Our Building.Woodsford Portland Street London. Dear Management Team, I am writing to make a formal complaint about the ongoing and increasingly unacceptable problems in our building. Residents have been reporting these issues almost every day, but unfortunately, nothing seems to be improving. We are extremely frustrated and disappointed with the current management and the lack of action from the officer responsible for looking after our building. The problems include: Lifts constantly breaking down: The lifts are repeatedly out of service. They are repaired one day, only to break down again the following day. This has been happening for years, and residents cannot continue living with this situation. Dog urine throughout the building: Some dog owners are allowing their dogs to urinate inside the lifts. Unfortunately, this behaviour has now spread to the staircases, corridors and other communal areas. There is a terrible smell, and the building is becoming increasingly unhygienic and unpleasant for everyone. Lack of CCTV: We desperately need CCTV cameras installed in communal areas to help identify those responsible for damaging and misusing shared spaces and to discourage this behaviour. We urgently request the following action: A new building management officer who is willing to take responsibility and deal with residents' concerns. A proper investigation into why the lifts keep breaking down, followed by a permanent solution rather than temporary repairs. CCTV installation in appropriate communal areas. Regular cleaning and proper monitoring of the building. Action against residents who allow their dogs to urinate in communal areas. A meeting with residents and the management team to discuss these serious concerns. We have reached a point where sending letters and making daily complaints is simply not enough. item.title: URGENT FORMAL COMPLAINT – Repeated Dog Fouling in the Building Lifts Stairs and Failure to Take Action, 16th November
item.description:
Email Subject URGENT FORMAL COMPLAINT – Repeated Dog Fouling in the Building Lift and Failure to Take Action Dear Southwark Council, I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding a serious and ongoing issue in our building. A dog owner is repeatedly allowing their dog to urinate inside the lift. This is happening almost every day and has been going on for years. The smell is absolutely disgusting and unbearable. Residents are unable to use the lift comfortably because of the strong smell of dog urine. This is completely unacceptable and is affecting the quality of life of everyone living in the building. We have reported this issue numerous times, but unfortunately, nothing has changed. Letters and warnings are clearly not working. We are extremely frustrated that, despite repeated complaints over such a long period, It is unfair that residents who respect their neighbours and their living environment have to put up with this behaviour every day. Everyone has the right to live in a clean, hygienic and pleasant environment. We are no longer asking for another letter to be sent. We are demanding real action. I would like Southwark Council to: Investigate this matter urgently and take appropriate action against the responsible dog owner. Enforce the relevant housing rules and consider penalties or other formal measures where appropriate. Arrange proper cleaning and disinfection of the lift to remove the smell of urine. Explain what action will be taken to prevent this from happening again. Provide residents with a clear response and a timescale for resolving this ongoing problem. How much longer are residents expected to tolerate this situation? This has been happening for years, and repeated reports have achieved absolutely nothing. Please take this complaint seriously.
